Diagnostics from posterior draws of the between-site SD

Source: R/draws.R
reliability_draws.Rd

Computes the diagnostics of the reliability profile at each posterior draw of the between-site standard deviation from another fit, such as a model fitted with Stan or brms, and summarizes them with their Monte Carlo error.

Usage

reliability_draws(
  x,
  ...,
  se = NULL,
  se2 = NULL,
  site = NULL,
  estimate = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  mean = NULL,
  variable = NULL,
  model_label = NULL,
  scale_label = NULL,
  target_label = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  threshold = 0.5
)

Arguments

x

Posterior draws of the between-site standard deviation: a numeric vector, an object that the posterior package can convert to draws (from Stan, CmdStan or brms, among others), or a fit of brms, from which the standard errors, the estimates and the sites are taken too.

...

Must be empty. The arguments after x are named, because an unnamed vector could hold standard errors or sampling variances.

se, se2

Standard errors or sampling variances of the site estimates, as in reliability_profile(). Give one of them.

site

Optional labels of the sites.

estimate

Optional estimates of the sites. With mean, the site table has the posterior means and intervals of the site effects.

data

Optional data frame in which se, se2, site and estimate are found, as in reliability_posterior().

mean

Optional draws of the mean of the effects, in the same order as the draws of x: a numeric vector, or with a draws object the name of its variable.

variable

Name of the variable of the standard deviation in a draws object, a string. NULL, the default, takes the one variable whose name starts with sd_ or is sigma_tau, tau or sigma; when there is not exactly one such variable, variable must be given.

model_label

A description of the model and the prior that gave the draws, a string, printed with the summaries.

scale_label, target_label

Optional strings that name the scale of the effects and the estimand at each site, as in reliability_posterior(). They are printed and used by report_text() and report_table().

level

Probability content of the posterior intervals, a number between 0 and 1.

threshold

Value of the informativeness whose posterior probability of being exceeded is reported, a number between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class reliability_draws, a list whose main components are

  • summary: a data frame with the mean, standard deviation, interval, Monte Carlo standard error (mcse) and effective sample size of the draws (ess) of each diagnostic, of sigma_tau and sigma_tau^2, and of the mean when its draws are given.

  • draws: the draws of sigma_tau and of the mean.

  • probability and probability_mcse: the proportion of draws with \(I\) above threshold, and its Monte Carlo standard error.

  • plugin: the diagnostics at the mean of the draws of sigma_tau^2.

  • se2, site, estimate, level, threshold, model_label and call: the inputs.

profile_summary(), site_table(), prob_above(), plugin_gap() and plot() take it.

Details

External-draw summaries are an experimental extension beyond Lee (2026); their interfaces may change in a later 0.x release.

The diagnostics depend on the draws only through the between-site standard deviation, so they apply to any posterior algorithm whose draws target the stated model and prior (Lee, 2026, Appendix D.3). Nothing is refitted: the model and the prior are those of the fit that gave the draws, and model_label names them for the printed output.

The posterior means are draw averages and come with their Monte Carlo standard errors. With the posterior package installed, the effective sample sizes of the draws (posterior::ess_mean()), which account for the autocorrelation of each chain, give the standard errors; otherwise the draws are treated as independent, with a message. For the integrals of the normal model with a flat or proper prior on the SD, reliability_posterior() has no Monte Carlo error.

A univariate Gaussian identity-link fit of brms of the form y | se(sei, sigma = FALSE) ~ 1 + (1 | group) is read directly. sigma = FALSE may be omitted. The response, known standard errors and grouping variable must be direct data columns, with one observation per group. The standard deviation comes from sd_<group>__Intercept and the common mean from b_Intercept. Extra residual variance, other families, additional group-level components, random slopes, distributional formulas, autocorrelation, smooths, Gaussian processes and latent measurement-error terms are not supported.

Gaussian models with fixed moderators can supply variance-based diagnostics and site reliabilities. Site effect estimates are omitted: a single common-mean draw cannot represent their site-specific population predictions. Giving mean for such a fit is an error.

The site summaries use the draws of the mean rather than the flat-prior formula: the posterior mean of site \(j\)'s effect averages \(\mu + S_j(\hat\tau_j - \mu)\) over the draws, and its interval is a quantile of the normal mixture over them.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

reliability_posterior(), whose integrals have no Monte Carlo error, and vignette("implementation") for a brms example.

Examples

# Draws of sigma_tau from some fit; here simulated for the example.
set.seed(1)
sigma_draws <- abs(rnorm(4000, 8, 4))
rd <- reliability_draws(sigma_draws, se = eight_schools$se,
                        model_label = "an example")
rd
#> Reliability profile of 8 sites (posterior draws from an example)
#> 4000 draws; Monte Carlo standard errors of the means in parentheses.
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean                95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.303    (0.0029)   0.005    0.637
#>   mean reliability           0.309    (0.0029)   0.005    0.631
#>   dispersion H               0.0201   (0.00014)  0.0005   0.0284
#>   concentration count J_eff  7.3      (0.0043)   6.8      7.8      of 8
#>   logit variance V           0.230               (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  8.10     (0.063)    0.844    16.1
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.162 (0.0057)
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.355
